title: [Bug] Pretokenized image requests can crash GLM MRoPE with a stale retokenized mask
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no existing report.
- [x] The vulnerable code is present on current `main`.
- [x] This report includes a minimal reproduction and affected revisions.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

Originally reported by @dzorlu in [this comment on #36833](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36833#issuecomment-5466686528), with a [minimal fix and workload reproduction](https://github.com/nanjiangwill/sglang/pull/1).

For a pretokenized image request, SGLang can pass two sequences with different provenance to GLM MRoPE:

- `input_ids`: the client's exact IDs, restored by `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` after image-token expansion;
- `attention_mask`: produced by the HF processor over `decode(input_ids)` re-tokenized.

Decode followed by tokenization is not length-preserving for noncanonical token sequences. For example, two separately sampled newline tokens can re-tokenize as one combined newline token. GLM MRoPE then indexes exact IDs of length `N+1` with a mask of length `N` and raises `IndexError`.

This is easier to hit in long multi-turn RL because sampled IDs are repeatedly reused as context. Short, single-turn VLM tests generally start with canonical IDs and do not expose it.

The issue is not specific to the Miles branch:

- current `main` restores exact IDs in [`base_processor.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py#L1702-L1739), then passes the processor mask in [`glm4v.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/glm4v.py#L102-L113);
- the same pattern is present in the GLM-5.3 implementation in [#36507](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36507): [exact-ID restoration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py#L1658-L1695) followed by the [retokenized mask](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/glm4v.py#L553-L564).

Although RL submits many rollouts concurrently, multimodal preprocessing is still per request: the HF processor receives `text=[input_text]`, and GLM flattens the result before restoring a `[1, sequence_length]` dimension for MRoPE. Continuous GPU batching happens later and does not add padding at this call site.

### How the mismatch was introduced

The GLM processor originally landed in [#8798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8798). At that point, both `input_ids` and `attention_mask` came directly from the HF processor, so they were aligned. Passing the processor mask to the GLM MRoPE helper was valid and preserved its support for padded batches.

[#26555](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26555) later added exact-ID restoration for pretokenized RL/VLM requests. The shared base processor began replacing the HF processor's `input_ids`, but the GLM consumer continued reading `attention_mask` from the old processor result. The two changes are independently reasonable; the bug is the missing ownership update between them.

### Reproduction

The tokenizer drift can be reproduced independently of the model backend:

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash")
newline = tokenizer.encode("\n", add_special_tokens=False)
exact_ids = tokenizer.encode("hello", add_special_tokens=False) + newline + newline
retokenized_ids = tokenizer.encode(
    tokenizer.decode(exact_ids), add_special_tokens=False
)

assert len(retokenized_ids) == len(exact_ids) - 1

ids = torch.tensor([exact_ids])
retokenized_mask = torch.ones((1, len(retokenized_ids)), dtype=torch.long)
ids[0][retokenized_mask[0] == 1]  # IndexError: mask and tensor shapes differ
```

The server path requires:

1. `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE=1` (the default);
2. a request containing exact `input_ids` and raw image data;
3. a noncanonical token sequence whose decode/tokenize round trip changes length.

The original report observed the failure in GLM-5.3 long multi-turn vision RL at approximately 8K and 36K tokens. The linked reproduction reports the same workload completing after the one-line change.

### Expected behavior

Any token-aligned mask passed to MRoPE must correspond to the final `input_ids`.

At the current GLM call site, each processor invocation contains exactly one unpadded sequence. Passing `attention_mask=None` is therefore behavior-preserving: `get_rope_index_glm4v` creates `torch.ones_like(total_input_ids)`, which is identical to the processor mask when lengths agree and correctly follows the final exact IDs when they do not.

This is a general fix for models using `Glm4vImageProcessor`, but the framework-level invariant is broader: if `process_and_combine_mm_data` replaces `input_ids`, downstream code should not consume token-aligned fields from the old processor result without rebuilding them.

A regression test should cover noncanonical pretokenized IDs plus an image and verify both exact-ID preservation and MRoPE position generation. A canonical-ID case should also verify that positions are unchanged.

### Fix scope

#### Immediate GLM fix

At this call site, pass `attention_mask=None` to `get_rope_index_glm4v`. The helper then creates `torch.ones_like(total_input_ids)` from the final exact IDs.

This is safe under the current `Glm4vImageProcessor` contract:

- processing is one request at a time;
- `padding=True` with `text=[input_text]` does not add padding;
- later continuous batching and RL training batching happen after MRoPE preprocessing;
- when the tokenizations already match, the processor mask is also all ones, so behavior is unchanged.

The current fix in #36833 follows this approach. Mask support should remain in `get_rope_index_glm4v`; only this unpadded call site should stop forwarding a potentially stale mask.

#### Principle-level fix

`process_and_combine_mm_data` should make the final `input_ids` and all token-aligned metadata share the same provenance. If it replaces processor-generated IDs with exact client IDs, it should also rebuild or invalidate the corresponding `attention_mask` and any other token-aligned fields.

One possible interface is to return an aligned final mask alongside the final IDs instead of requiring model-specific processors to read it from the raw HF result:

```python
mm_items, input_ids, attention_mask, processor_output = (
    process_and_combine_mm_data(...)
)
```

For today's per-request unpadded path, that mask is simply `torch.ones_like(final_input_ids)`. If true padded processor batching is added later, the base layer can construct the mask from the final sequence lengths after rebuilding/padding the IDs.

The important invariant is:

```text
final input_ids and every token-aligned tensor must describe the same sequence
```

This would remove the same class of stale-metadata bugs from downstream multimodal processors rather than fixing each consumer separately.

### Environment

```text
Model: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash
SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE: 1 (default)
Affected current main: 512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45
Affected #36507 head: 7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362
Miles-branch fix currently tracked in: #36833
```

The exception occurs during CPU-side multimodal preprocessing, before model execution or continuous batching, so it is independent of the GPU and attention backend.
